newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bangkok Bank profit hit by slow lending.
newsitem.headline: Bangkok Bank profit hit by slow lending.

text.p: Thailand's top bank, Bangkok Bank Plc, reported slower first half profit growth this year against that recorded in the corresponding year-ago period due to the effects of the central bank's tight monetary policy, stock analysts said on Tuesday.
The bank said its first half profit rose seven percent to 10.34 billion baht compared with 9.68 billion or a 15 percent jump in the same period in 1995.

Analysts said the Bank of Thailand (BOT) had in the first half of this year used a high interest rates policy to fight rising prices which also squeezed lending by financial institutions like Bangkok Bank.
"Bangkok Bank and other commercial banks' lending was very slow in the first half as a result of the BOT's tight policy," Thanawat Patchimkul, a banking analyst at Seamico Securities, told Reuters.
Kasem Prunratanamala, an analyst at James Capel Asia, expected Bangkok Bank's net profit to grow only seven percent in all of 1996 compared 13.5 percent growth in 1995.
Bangkok Bank announced 1995 net profit of 19.7 billion baht compared with 17.36 billion baht in 1994.
"The bank's profit in the first half is in line with my expectation. But it's very difficult for the bank to maintain earnings growth above 10 percent," Kasem said.

Thanawat said Thai commercial banks' earnings are expected to improve in the second half this year following an apparent, easier BOT monetary policy and expectations interest rates will fall by the end of this year.
Analysts said they expected rates to drop by up to 50 basis points by the end of this year. Current lending rates range from 13.25-13.75 percent, among the highest in Southeast Asia..
"The interest spread of most banks will improve in the second half as deposit interest are being cut. While any further reduction in lending rates will help boost their lending," Thanawat said.
Bangkok Bank said in a statement that its assets at the end of June rose 12 percent to 1.1 trillion baht from 986.23 billion during the same period last year.
Total deposits at the end of the period increased by 16.4 percent to 831.33 billion baht while outstanding loans were up 9.5 percent to 891.72 billion baht.
